header: IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE
Muhammad Khawar Butt Vs. Assistant Commissioner etc.
Order with signature of judge, and that of parties or counsel,
18.11.2026. Mr. Riasat Noor Zaman, Advocate for petitioner
Ch. Najam Ul Hassan, AAG with Fakhar Raza, AD. (Legal)
body: Muhammad Khawar Butt (petitioner) has called in question the impugned order dated 20.01.2023 passed by respondent No.1/Assistant Commissioner/Collector, Sadar Sub-Division, Faisalabad, and order dated 31.07.2025 passed by respondent No.2/Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faisalabad, whereby his grievance regarding the alleged unauthorized issuance of a Fard Performa by respondent No.4 (Muhammad Riaz Gujjar) in favour of respondent No.5 (Usman Hanif) in respect of property measuring 18 Marlas, comprised in Khewat No.1837 and Khatooni No.2045, situated at Makkah City, Faisalabad, was declined.

2. Briefly, the facts giving rise to instant petition are that petitioner claimed ownership of the aforementioned property and alleges that respondent No.4 (Muhammad Riaz Gujjar), being the concerned Patwari, had unlawfully issued a Fard Performa in favour of respondent No.5 (Usman Hanif, Advocate) without his consent and authority. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioner approached respondent No.3, Director, Anti-Corruption Establishment, Faisalabad Region, lodging a complaint, where the matter was referred to revenue authorities for inquiry and report. The concerned officials recorded the statements of petitioner and respondent No.4, besides undertaking the requisite inquiry. Eventually, respondent No.1, vide order dated 20.01.2023, consigned petitioner's application to record, whereafter petitioner challenged the said order before respondent No.2, who, vide order dated 31.07.2025, also consigned the matter. Hence, instant constitutional petition.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner contends that the impugned orders have been passed without proper appreciation of the material available on record; that respondent No.4 had admitted issuance of disputed Fard Performa, which itself constituted sufficient material to initiate disciplinary and penal proceedings against him; and the revenue authorities failed to appreciate the unauthorized exercise of his official authority and thereby deprived the petitioner of protection guaranteed under the Constitution. It is further contended that the impugned orders are arbitrary, non-speaking and suffer from material illegality, thus warranting interference by this Court. Conversely, the learned Law Officer opposed the petition in hand and prayed for its dismissal.

5. The controversy, in substance, emanates from the petitioner's allegation that the concerned Patwari issued a Fard Performa in favour of respondent No.5 without his consent or authorization. A perusal of record reflects that petitioner had already approached the Anti-Corruption Establishment, whereupon the matter was referred to the revenue authorities for inquiry, wherein the statements of concerned persons were recorded and matter was thoroughly examined by the competent revenue officers. It is, therefore, evident that the petitioner's grievance was not left unattended; rather, it was subjected to scrutiny by the relevant authorities. A perusal of the impugned orders reveals that the revenue authorities considered the nature of the petitioner's grievance, examined the available revenue record and the material collected during the inquiry. It is also significant that the petitioner has not been able to identify any specific finding in the impugned orders which is demonstrably contrary to the available record or suffers from any jurisdictional defect. The mere fact that the authorities did not accept the petitioner's version or grant the relief sought by him does not render their decisions arbitrary or illegal. The constitutional jurisdiction of this Court is not intended to substitute its opinion for that of the competent administrative authorities in every matter where a party remains dissatisfied with the outcome of an inquiry; interference is warranted only on limited grounds [ ]. So far as the petitioner's claim of ownership is concerned, any substantive controversy relating to title, possession or competing proprietary claims is to be determined by the competent forum in accordance with law. The present proceedings cannot be converted into an independent adjudication of such disputed questions of fact [ ], particularly when no tangible alteration of the petitioner's ownership rights through the impugned Fard Performa has been established, as entries in the revenue record neither create nor extinguish proprietary rights [ ]. Needless to observe, the petitioner shall remain at liberty to avail any remedy otherwise available to him under the law, should his proprietary rights actually be infringed.

[ ] M. Hamad Hassan v. Mst. Isma Bukhari and 2 others (2023 SCMR 1434) [ ] Special Secretary-II (Law & Order), Home & Tribal Affairs Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar and others v. Fayyaz Dawar (2023 SCMR 1442); Chairperson TEVTA v. Shahid Saleem & others (C.P.L.A No.1333 of 2025…..This judgment is passed by Hon’ble Federal Constitutional Court wherein, at para 4, the Court observed in following way “ However, we observe that the observations would run counter to the scope of the Constitutional jurisdiction which expressly debars the resolution of controversial and disputed questions of fact.” [ ] Haji Muhammad Yunis (deceased) through legal heirs and another v. Mst. Farukh Sultan and others (2022 SCMR 1282)

6. In view of above, petitioner has failed to make out a case for invoking the extraordinary constitutional jurisdiction of this Court under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973. Consequently, this constitutional petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed. (Khalid Ibn-i-Aziz)
